_about: Curated data for moon.html (Moon explorer). Coordinates are selenographic (IAU mean-Earth/polar-axis frame), latitude north positive, longitude EAST positive, degrees. Dates are UTC landing/impact dates. Sources are listed per record and in 'sources'.

sources.alsj: Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, 'Landing Site Coordinates' (LRO-derived), https://www.nasa.gov/history/alsj/alsjcoords.html
sources.lroc2016: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC), '2016 LROC Coordinates of Robotic Spacecraft', https://www.lroc.asu.edu/data/support/downloads/2016_LROC_Coordinates_of_Robotic_Spacecraft.pdf
sources.nssdc: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), lunar mission pages and 'Lunar artifact impacts', https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunar_artifact_impacts.html
sources.wiki: Wikipedia mission articles (coordinates as published there, citing LROC / the operating agency)
sources.lroc: LROC image releases of recent landers (lroc.im-ldi.com / lroc.asu.edu)
sources.nasa_se: NASA Goddard eclipse website (F. Espenak): Solar Eclipses 2021-2030 and 2031-2040, https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEdecade/SEdecade2021.html , https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEdecade/SEdecade2031.html
sources.nasa_le: NASA Goddard eclipse website: Lunar Eclipses 2021-2030, https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/LEdecade/LEdecade2021.html
sources.espenak_phases: F. Espenak, Phases of the Moon 2001-2100 (astropixels.com)

sites.name: Luna 2
sites.summary: First human-made object to reach another world. Its impact east of Archimedes, between Autolycus and Aristillus, confirmed the Moon has no significant magnetic field.

sites.name: Ranger 7
sites.summary: Returned 4,308 television pictures in its last 17 minutes before impact, the first close-ups of the lunar surface. The spot was named Mare Cognitum (the Known Sea).

sites.name: Luna 9
sites.summary: First soft landing on another world and the first photographs from the lunar surface, proving the regolith could bear a spacecraft's weight.

sites.name: Surveyor 1
sites.summary: First United States soft landing. Sent 11,237 photos from inside the flooded crater Flamsteed P in Oceanus Procellarum and scouted terrain for Apollo.

sites.name: Luna 13
sites.summary: Landed in Oceanus Procellarum and used a spring-loaded penetrometer and a radiation densitometer to measure the soil's strength and density.

sites.name: Surveyor 3
sites.summary: First lander to dig into the Moon with a scoop. Apollo 12 landed 180 m away in 1969 and brought its camera back to Earth.

sites.name: Surveyor 5
sites.summary: Made the first chemical analysis of lunar soil with an alpha-scattering instrument, finding basalt in Mare Tranquillitatis, about 25 km from the future Apollo 11 site.

sites.name: Surveyor 6
sites.summary: In Sinus Medii, near the centre of the near side. It fired its engines to hop 2.5 m: the first lift-off from the Moon.

sites.name: Surveyor 7
sites.summary: The only Surveyor sent to the highlands, on the ejecta blanket north of Tycho. It saw laser beams fired from Earth.

sites.name: Apollo 11
sites.crew: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin (surface); Michael Collins (Command Module Columbia)
sites.summary: The first people on the Moon. Eagle landed with about 25 seconds of hover propellant left; 2 h 31 min outside, 21.5 kg of samples, and the first Lunar Laser Ranging retroreflector.

sites.name: Apollo 12
sites.crew: Charles "Pete" Conrad, Alan Bean (surface); Richard Gordon (Command Module Yankee Clipper)
sites.summary: A pinpoint landing within walking distance of Surveyor 3, proving Apollo could land where it aimed. Two moonwalks, 34.4 kg of samples.

sites.name: Luna 16
sites.summary: First robotic sample return: a drill took 101 g of basalt from Mare Fecunditatis and a small ascent stage flew it straight home.

sites.name: Luna 17 · Lunokhod 1
sites.summary: Delivered Lunokhod 1, the first remotely driven rover on another world. Drivers on Earth steered it 10.5 km over ten months. Its French-built retroreflector was lost until LRO images located it in 2010 and it now returns laser pulses again.

sites.name: Apollo 14
sites.crew: Alan Shepard, Edgar Mitchell (surface); Stuart Roosa (Command Module Kitty Hawk)
sites.summary: Took Apollo 13's target, the Fra Mauro formation of Imbrium ejecta. Used a hand cart (the Modular Equipment Transporter), left a laser retroreflector, and Shepard hit two golf balls.

sites.name: Apollo 15
sites.crew: David Scott, James Irwin (surface); Alfred Worden (Command Module Endeavour)
sites.summary: First mission with the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV): 27.9 km of driving along Hadley Rille and the Apennine front. Found the 4-billion-year-old 'Genesis Rock' and left the largest retroreflector (300 corner cubes).

sites.name: Luna 20
sites.summary: Returned 55 g of highland soil from the Apollonius highlands between Mare Fecunditatis and Mare Crisium.

sites.name: Apollo 16
sites.crew: John Young, Charles Duke (surface); Ken Mattingly (Command Module Casper)
sites.summary: The only Apollo landing in the central highlands. The Lunar Roving Vehicle carried the crew 26.7 km; they found impact breccias rather than the volcanic rocks geologists expected.

sites.name: Apollo 17
sites.crew: Eugene Cernan, Harrison Schmitt (surface); Ronald Evans (Command Module America)
sites.summary: The last crewed landing so far. Geologist Harrison Schmitt found orange volcanic glass; 35.7 km of Lunar Roving Vehicle traverses and a record 110.5 kg of samples.

sites.name: Luna 21 · Lunokhod 2
sites.summary: Lunokhod 2 drove about 39 km in four months, a record that stood until 2014. Its retroreflector is still used for Lunar Laser Ranging.

sites.name: Luna 24
sites.summary: Drilled a 2 m core in Mare Crisium and returned 170 g of it: the last lunar sample return for 44 years.

sites.name: Chang'e 3 · Yutu
sites.summary: China's first lunar landing and the first soft landing anywhere since 1976. The Yutu rover's ground-penetrating radar mapped buried lava layers.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 · Yutu-2
sites.site: Von Kármán crater, South Pole–Aitken basin
sites.summary: First landing on the far side, talking to Earth through the Queqiao relay satellite beyond the Moon. Yutu-2 became the longest-lived lunar rover.

sites.name: Beresheet
sites.summary: First privately funded lunar landing attempt. A gyroscope fault and main engine shutdown during descent ended in a crash; LRO imaged the scar.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-2 · Vikram
sites.summary: The lander deviated from its braking profile and hit the surface near the south polar highlands; the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter still works.

sites.name: Chang'e 5
sites.summary: Returned 1,731 g of the youngest lunar basalt ever sampled (about 2 billion years old), with a robotic rendezvous in lunar orbit.

sites.name: HAKUTO-R Mission 1
sites.summary: Its altitude estimate went wrong over a crater rim; the lander ran out of propellant while still about 5 km up and fell inside Atlas crater.

sites.name: Luna 25
sites.summary: Russia's first lunar mission since 1976. An over-long orbit-lowering burn sent it into the surface; LRO found the new 10 m crater.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 · Vikram & Pragyan
sites.site: Statio Shiv Shakti, south polar region
sites.summary: India's first soft landing and the closest yet to the south pole at the time. The Pragyan rover measured sulfur in the soil; Vikram made a small hop.

sites.name: SLIM
sites.summary: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM) made Japan the fifth country to soft-land, within about 55 m of its target, though it tipped onto its nose after losing an engine nozzle.

sites.name: IM-1 · Odysseus
sites.summary: First commercial soft landing and the first United States landing since 1972, under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS). A laser rangefinder was left disabled, and Odysseus landed on its side but kept working for days.

sites.name: Chang'e 6
sites.summary: First sample return from the far side: 1,935.3 g collected in the Apollo basin, returned to Earth on 25 June 2024.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
sites.summary: The first fully successful commercial landing: upright and on target. It operated through a full lunar day, drilled heat-flow probes, and filmed a sunset from the surface.

sites.name: IM-2 · Athena
sites.site: Near Mons Mouton, south polar region
sites.summary: Landed in a crater about 250 m from its target and came to rest on its side in the cold dark, the southernmost landing so far. It ran for a little under a day.

sites.name: HAKUTO-R Mission 2 · Resilience
sites.summary: Its laser rangefinder returned measurements too late during descent; the lander could not slow enough and struck Mare Frigoris. LRO imaged the impact site.

sites.name: Artemis III (planned)
sites.site: One of nine candidate regions within 6° of the south pole
sites.crew: Four astronauts, two to the surface (crew not yet named)
sites.summary: PLANNED, not flown. NASA has named nine candidate landing regions near the south pole (among them Peak near Cabeus B, Haworth, Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton Plateau, Mons Mouton, Nobile Rim 1 and 2, de Gerlache Rim 2 and Slater Plain), chosen for long sunlight, Earth visibility and nearby permanently shadowed craters that may hold water ice.
